How To Master The Art Of Being
Able To Talk To Anyone
Start with something you both see. A long queue, loud music, a funny sign. Shared surroundings give you an easy, natural first sentence with anyone.
Be genuinely interested in their world. A mechanic, a nurse, a student. Everyone knows things you don't, and curiosity makes people open up quickly.
Adjust your pace to theirs. Slow and calm with a shy person, lively with an energetic one. Matching their rhythm makes them feel comfortable fast.
Use humour gently. A small joke about yourself or the situation breaks the ice. Avoid teasing people you've just met, it can easily go wrong.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. With more topics in your head, you'll find common ground with almost anyone.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. With more topics in your head, you'll find common ground with anyone.

slides.texte_overlay: Be okay with people who don't want to talk. Not everyone will. A friendly smile and moving on is part of the art, never a failure.
Practise in low-pressure places. Shops, cafés, waiting rooms. Small daily conversations build the skill until talking to anyone feels natural.
